- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) and supply net is negative, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >+5% from prior 30d avg), model often overshoots; apply downward correction of 10–20% in next 5–7d horizon.
- In high-bearish event contexts (bearish > 30, supply net < -15), model underestimates; adjust forecast upward by 2–5% to reflect market stress reversal.
- If sentiment history shows strong bullish momentum followed by bearish reversal, model often fails to retrace; add mean-reversion buffer (e.g., 1–2% per 3d) toward prior 10d average.
- For 30d forecasts with high event count and negative supply net, model tends to be overly conservative; increase baseline by 1–3% to account for event-driven volatility.
- When sentiment is low (≤0.33) and supply net is negative, model underestimates; apply upward bias of 1–3% to reflect subdued market sentiment.
- In multi-event periods (e.g., 20+ events/30d), model often fails to capture event clustering; use rolling 7d average to smooth event-driven noise before forecasting.
